articles.title: '20 markets, Rs 12,000cr trade at stake': Delhi traders urge Sonia Gandhi to defer Rahul Gandhi's November 1 rally
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) in Delhi on Friday urged senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi to postpone the party's proposed mega
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) in Delhi on Friday urged senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi to postpone the party's proposed mega rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, warning that it could disrupt business worth Rs 10,000-12,000 crore across 20 markets in the national capital.The trade body said the rally, proposed by leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, comes at a crucial time when markets are preparing for the Diwali shopping season.The trade body warned of severe economic losses during the peak festive shopping season.The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) said the rally is expected to draw around 10 lakh people and 15,000 to 20,000 vehicles to central Delhi. It warned that the large gathering could lead to severe traffic congestion and affect the movement of goods and shoppers across the markets."We demand to reschedule the mega-rally of 1 million (10 lakh) people, planned for November 1, to a date after Diwali; lack of parking for 15,000–20,000 vehicles could lead to a total gridlock, akin to a lockdown," the CTI urged in its letter to Sonia Gandhi.The traders' body said the rally is planned at a crucial time for businesses, with Dhanteras falling on November 6 and Diwali on November 8. It said November 1 is expected to be one of the busiest days for transporting festive goods and for shoppers visiting the markets.CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said traders were worried about the possible impact on their livelihoods and stressed that the appeal was not against the rally."We are not opposing the rally; we are making a heartfelt plea to protect our livelihoods during the peak Diwali season," stated CTI Chairman Brijesh Goyal."These 20 markets are not merely marketplaces; they are the heartbeat of Delhi. They generate a daily turnover of 10,000 to 12,000 crore rupees, and Dhanteras falls on November 6th. Traders are anxious: if a lockdown-like gridlock hits central Delhi on October 31st and November 1st, how will the goods for Dhanteras be transported in and out?" Goyal added."Dhanteras falls on November 6, and Diwali is on November 8; November 1 is the busiest day for preparations... If 1 million people and 15,000–20,000 vehicles arrive in Central Delhi on November 1, the daily business turnover of Rs 10,000–12,000 crore across 20 historic markets will come to a complete standstill," Goyal noted.Parking and traffic concernsIn its letter, the CTI listed four major concerns. The first was the lack of parking space at Ramlila Maidan."Where will 15,000–20,000 vehicles be parked? Ramlila Maidan does not even have the capacity to park 200 large buses."The second concern was the possible disruption to 20 wholesale and retail markets within a 5-km radius of the venue. The CTI said these markets together record daily business worth Rs 10,000-12,000 crore.The markets include Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazar, Connaught Place, Palika Bazar, Janpath, Bhagirath Palace, Khari Baoli, Kashmiri Gate, Naya Bazar, Lajpat Rai Market, Chawri Bazar, Kinari Bazar, Dariba Kalan, Ballimaran, Fatehpuri, Tilak Bazar, Karol Bagh, Jama Masjid, Nabi Karim, Gaffar Market, Ajmeri Gate-Paharganj and Daryaganj.The traders' body also warned that traffic restrictions could begin well before the rally. It said buses and other vehicles may start arriving at Delhi's borders, including Singhu, Tikri, Ghazipur and Badarpur, from the afternoon of October 31. Barricades could also be put up along Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg and JLN Marg by the evening.The CTI said transporters had already begun refusing to send vehicles to the markets from October 31.It also cited the traffic disruption during an earlier protest as a reason for concern."On October 10th, with only 5,000 to 7,000 people gathering at Jantar Mantar, central Delhi remained gridlocked for eight hours. Now, 1 million (10 lakh) people are expected to arrive."The CTI said the markets, some of which are up to 300 years old, supply goods to different parts of the country. It added that their operations depend on around 5,000 trucks and tempos arriving daily from 56 industrial areas, including Narela, Bawana, Okhla, Mayapuri, Mundka, Udyog Nagar and Mangolpuri.CTI suggests two alternativesTo avoid disruption during the festive season, the CTI has suggested two options. It has asked the organisers to postpone the rally until after November 10 or shift it to Burari Maidan if the November 1 date cannot be changed.The rally, called the 'Chalo Dilli Ramlila March', has been organised by the opposition INDIA bloc to protest against alleged vote tampering.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has said the march is not limited to any one political party and has appealed to people to join it."Chalo Dilli Ramlila March, it is a march to save democracy, to stop vote theft, to save the Constitution. This is not a march of any one political party; it is a march of the soul of India. All the people who are fed up with Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, and Gyanesh Kumar, all the people who want to save democracy, who want to protect the Constitution, you all come," Rahul Gandhi stated.The letter to Sonia Gandhi came after the trade body had also written to Rahul Gandhi, urging him to postpone the rally to avoid disrupting business during the festive season.With less than 48 hours left before the rally, traders are waiting for a response from the Congress leadership to their request.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A Bengaluru woman breaks down her household help expenses; spends ₹42,100 every month on household help; her annual bill crosses ₹5 lakh, and there is more
articles.summary: For many families living in Bengaluru, the capital of Karnataka, managing a household is no longer just about paying rent or EMIs or paying electricity
articles.body: For many families living in Bengaluru, the capital of Karnataka, managing a household is no longer just about paying rent or EMIs or paying electricity bills. There is a substantial expense that quietly adds to the monthly budget in the name of household help. It includes nannies, cooks, deep-cleaning services and more. And it’s not an insignificant amount for sure.A recent Instagram post by Bengaluru-based creator Sakshi Mehra (@sassy.sakshi), has caught people’s attention where she breaks down her monthly household expenses living in Bengaluru. Sharing a detailed breakdown, the woman revealed that the monthly bill comes to ₹42,100 which translates into ₹5,05,200 a year, just for domestic help.And this clearly does not include monthly ration, daily groceries, electricity and gas bill, laundry, repairs and more.How much does household help cost in BengaluruThe creator says she lives near Bellandur. Household help rates can differ depending on the locality, apartment and working hours, among other factors.The monthly breakup:Childcare: ₹23,000 a monthCook: ₹7,500 a monthRegular household cleaning: ₹5,500 a monthDeep-cleaning of two bathrooms: ₹1,500 a monthDeep-cleaning of the balcony: ₹600 a monthDusting the car: ₹1,500Sundays cleaning: ₹1,000 a monthSo for her, the biggest expense is childcare. The family pays ₹23,000 a month to a nanny who looks after their kid from 9 am to 7 pm. With a 10-hour daily arrangement, childcare alone accounts for more than half of the total budget.The cook takes ₹7,500 a month and prepares breakfast, lunch and dinner. The menu includes breakfast options such as poha, upma and oats; one vegetable dish and six rotis for lunch; and dal, another vegetable dish and three rotis for dinner.Regular household cleaning costs another ₹5,500 a month. Beyond this, the family spends ₹1,500 on monthly kitchen deep-cleaning and dusting service.Deep-cleaning of two bathrooms costs an additional ₹1,500, while washing the balcony once a month costs approximately ₹600.Dusting the car costs ₹1,500.Since all the regular household workers take Sundays off, the family either eats out or manages its meals themselves. For cleaning, they turn to online cleaning services, spending approximately ₹250 for a few hours of assistance which adds to around ₹1,000 a month.While alone these amounts may not appear extraordinary, when added together, they reveal how expensive it can be to outsource the services.Why childcare changes the household budgetOne interesting aspect of the breakdown is the childcare which is ₹23,000 a month. For families with young children, this is often an essential expense rather than an optional convenience.A nanny working for 10 hours a day provides parents with the time and support needed to manage their professional responsibilities, household commitments and personal lives.The hidden cost of running a homeMehra's post also brings attention to a larger conversation around the cost of domestic services in Bengaluru. Household help rates are not uniform across the city. The number of family members, size of the apartment, working hours, responsibilities and neighbourhood can all influence what a household pays.The issue has also featured in local conversations about domestic workers' wages. In August 2024, The Times of India reported on disagreements between some resident welfare associations and domestic workers over salary rates in Bengaluru apartments, with rising living costs adding to the debate.Mehra's calculation, however, does not represent the average household expenditure in Bengaluru. The post has also invited other Bengaluru residents, particularly mothers, to share how much they spend on household help and which neighbourhood they live in.Perhaps the most striking takeaway is that the ₹42,100 figure is not the cost of running the entire household. It is only the cost of getting help to run it. For families with young children, the calculation is also about more than money. It is about buying time, finding reliable support and making everyday life a little more manageable.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: US Federal appeals court revives religious groups’ legal challenge to immigration enforcement at churches, synagogues and mosques; what the ruling means for worshippers
articles.summary: Immigration enforcement at churches, synagogues and mosques is back before the courts after a federal appeals court revived a religious freedom lawsuit
articles.body: Immigration enforcement at churches, synagogues and mosques is back before the courts after a federal appeals court revived a religious freedom lawsuit against the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS). In January 2025, the department scrapped the sensitive locations policy, which for more than thirty years had limited immigration operations at places of worship, schools and funerals. Twenty-seven Judeo-Christian organisations, representing millions of worshippers, sued under the First Amendment, the Religious Freedom Restoration Act and the Administrative Procedure Act. Their congregations serve undocumented immigrants through worship, food pantries, legal advice and job training, now with enforcement left to office-level supervisors’ case-by-case discretion.From strict approval rules to supervisor discretion: what changed for places of worshipThe safeguard dates to 1993, when the government directed immigration authorities to avoid arrests and tightly control investigations at schools, places of worship, funerals and religious ceremonies. According to the appeals court opinion published by Justia, the latest version arrived in 2021 under then-Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas. It told officers to avoid action at or near such places to the fullest extent possible and demanded prior approval from agency headquarters or its delegates. It allowed exceptions only in emergencies such as national security threats, imminent violence, destruction of evidence or hot pursuit of a public safety threat.Acting Secretary Benjamine Huffman replaced it with an instruction to use discretion and common sense. Eleven days later, Acting Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Director Caleb Vitello rejected fixed rules, leaving office-level supervisors to decide case by case, verbally or in writing. The DHS said in a press release that immigrants it classed as criminals could no longer shelter in schools and churches to avoid arrest.Raids, surveillance and falling attendance: the evidence the faith groups put before the courtThe plaintiffs comprise sixteen national or regional denominational bodies and eleven associations, among them the Union for Reform Judaism, the Latino Christian National Network and the Rabbinical Assembly. Their traditions range from Quakers and Mennonites to Catholics, Evangelicals, Pentecostals and United Methodists. Leaders and congregants filed declarations, and members of all but one plaintiff reported falling attendance at services and community events as worshippers feared enforcement.The court record also lists specific incidents after the rescission: a raid at a church linked to a plaintiff, a raid next door to another, a raid at a church outside the lawsuit, and surveillance at or near three plaintiff-linked churches. The North Georgia Conference of the United Methodist Church said in a declaration that agents entered a church daycare office looking for a staff member they believed to be undocumented. The Episcopal Church said agents photographed people queuing at a food pantry hosted by a California congregation.Why the appeals court rejected a gun-case test and saw a credible threat to worshippersThe district court refused the groups’ request for a temporary order, known as a preliminary injunction, ruling their fears too speculative. Its reasoning turned on standing, the legal right to sue, which requires a harm that is imminent, linked to the policy and fixable by a court. It borrowed a test from firearms cases that asks whether plaintiffs were singled out for enforcement.Bloomberg Law reported that the Justice Department made a similar argument on appeal, saying the groups needed specific information that a particular church was about to be raided. Two judges appeared sceptical at oral argument in early February, with one asking how churches could possibly have such insider knowledge of upcoming operations.Circuit Judge Florence Pan, joined by Circuit Judge Robert Wilkins, wrote for the appeals court that the firearms test does not suit a challenge to an agency policy that burdens religious expression. Applying the Supreme Court’s credible threat standard instead, she wrote that the government had not disavowed enforcement at such places. The government’s own statements said agents believed the rescission would free them to pursue more undocumented immigrants, and operations had begun near plaintiffs’ congregations as a direct result of the change. Reinstating the old guidance, she wrote, need only prevent a single operation at a single congregation. A judicial warrant requirement would force agents to show a judge probable cause, slowing and deterring operations.Judge Rao’s dissent: The argument that restoring the old memo would not change enforcementCircuit Judge Neomi Rao argued that the 2021 guidance never limited the government’s legal authority or enforcement discretion, so predicting its effect is speculation. She described its rescission as one relatively minor part of a broader policy of increasing immigration enforcement. The dissent noted that the district court found only one enforcement action at the hundreds of member congregations, and three instances at or near any place of worship nationwide in the first ten weeks. It added that courts cannot direct how the executive branch prioritises enforcement. It also said a judicial warrant requirement would exceed judicial powers and is barred by a federal law limiting lower courts’ power to restrain parts of the immigration code.Pan answered that the dissent rested on a mistaken belief that the old memo was non-binding. Courts generally assume agencies follow their announced policies, she wrote, and otherwise the administration would not have needed to rescind it. The majority added that the lawsuit was filed less than three weeks after the rescission, so even a few incidents point to increased enforcement.What happens next as the case returns to the district court, and what the ruling leaves openThe split decision, handed down on 20 October 2026, reverses the denial of the temporary order and sends the motion back to the district court for further consideration. It does not decide whether the policy is lawful. The panel rested on a single theory of harm, the threat of immigration enforcement at congregations. It left the groups’ claims about falling attendance, moral dilemmas and security costs undecided. It also declined to say whether a judicial warrant requirement is permissible, because neither side had argued that point.Maryland and Massachusetts cases test the same policy as scrutiny of immigration tactics growsBloomberg Law reported that the ruling arrives amid heightened scrutiny of ICE tactics. Two Americans were fatally shot in Minnesota during an enforcement surge, and congressional gridlock over Democrats’ demands to rein in the agency caused a partial government shutdown and a funding lapse for the DHS earlier this year. Kelsi Brown Corkran of Georgetown Law’s Institute for Constitutional Advocacy and Protection, lead counsel for the religious associations, told the publication by email that the decision was “an important victory for the millions of people of faith” in the coalition. A Justice Department spokesperson declined to comment.Other organisations are challenging the same change in federal courts in Maryland and Massachusetts. In August, six months after oral argument in the Washington case, the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit upheld a ruling barring federal immigration operations at certain houses of worship. That case was brought by the Philadelphia Yearly Meeting of the Religious Society of Friends, and the order requires the DHS to revert to the 2021 guidance at those plaintiffs’ houses of worship. In February, a Massachusetts federal judge temporarily blocked enforcement, absent emergencies, in or around certain houses of worship that sued, and that case is pending on appeal. The dissent noted that courts hearing similar cases have found plaintiffs likely to succeed on the merits yet refused to order judicial warrants.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.body: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos says he can’t tell whether artificial intelligence is in a bubble, but he knows what he would tell someone living off their savings, Benzinga reports. As excitement around artificial intelligence continues to fuel massive investments and soaring valuations across the technology sector, Jeff Bezos says retirees should resist the temptation to bet on individual AI stocks and instead follow a strategy long championed by Warren Buffett: buy the broader market. Speaking in an interview with Fox News host Bret Baier recently, the Amazon founder was asked whether the AI industry is currently experiencing a bubble. Bezos said it was difficult to know with certainty but stressed that the underlying technology is undeniably real. "It's hard to know," Bezos said when asked about a potential AI bubble. "What I do know is the technology is real."Jeff Bezos believes good ideas and bad ideas get funded togetherBezos said the problem in periods like this is that every experiment gets funded, the good ideas along with the bad. In the middle of the frenzy, he said, it is hard for investors to tell them apart. Speculators can lose money when enthusiasm runs ahead of results, he argued, but the inventions themselves don’t disappear. In his view, that makes the situation tricky for investors and good for society."Every experiment gets funded, the good ideas and the bad ideas," Bezos said, adding that it can be difficult for investors to distinguish between winners and losers while the boom is unfolding.Trillions being spent on AI infrastructureThe comments from Bezos come as investment in AI infrastructure is growing continuously. As per the report, basket of 41 AI-linked companies tracked by JPMorgan Chase accounts for roughly 49% of the market value of the S&P 500, highlighting the growing concentration of investor interest in the sector. Major tech companies like Google, Apple, Nvidia, Microsoft and Amazon have become the biggest gainers of the AI boom. The report further adds that the world's largest hyperscale technology companies are said to spend around $800 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026, even though the long-term revenue impact from AI investments remains difficult to quantify.Jeff Bezos echoes Warren Buffett's long-standing adviceWhen Baier shifted the discussion to a practical question and asked whether he would recommend retirees own AI stocks today, Bezos offered a straightforward answer. "I would usually tell a retiree to buy the S&P 500," he said. The advice given by Bezos mirrors the recommendations made by Warren Buffett, chairman emeritus of Berkshire Hathaway, who has repeatedly advocated low-cost investments tied to the S&P 500 as a simple way for long-term investors to build wealth without attempting to pick individual winners. The index already includes major AI beneficiaries such as Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon and Apple, allowing investors to gain exposure to the sector while maintaining diversification.You use AI every day. articles.title: Family gets no proper food, 11-month-old baby not given milk on 15-hour Delhi-Melbourne Singapore Airlines flight in 2020; 6 years later, airline ordered to pay Rs 50,000 plus litigation expenses
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A passenger's complaint that his family, including an 11-month-old baby, was not served adequate food on a 15-hour flight has led the Punjab
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A passenger's complaint that his family, including an 11-month-old baby, was not served adequate food on a 15-hour flight has led the Punjab State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission to hold Singapore Airlines liable for deficiency in service, according to a report by Bar and Bench.The commission ruled that an airline cannot escape responsibility for providing regular meals simply because passengers have not asked for special food.It also pointed out that Singapore Airlines had failed to establish that the family was served adequate food during the journey.The dispute dates back to March 4, 2020, when Jaspreet Singh's wife, mother-in-law and infant daughter flew from Delhi to Melbourne.Singh alleged that the family was not provided proper meals during the journey and that even milk for his 11-month-old daughter was not made available.After Singh raised the issue through an email, the airline initially promised to look into the complaint. However, its subsequent response was that the passengers had not placed a request for vegetarian or special meals. It also asked Singh to take up the matter with his travel agent.Unhappy with the response, Singh approached the district consumer commission in Ropar. He sought a refund of Rs 1.25 lakh towards the tickets and ₹10 lakh in compensation.In January 2023, the district commission ordered Singapore Airlines and the travel agent to refund the ticket fare with 7% annual interest. It also awarded Rs 25,000 as compensation and Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses.The airline challenged the decision before the state commission, maintaining that no special meal request had been made and that food from its regular menu had been served.The state commission rejected this argument, holding that passengers need not request special meals to be entitled to ordinary food on a long-duration flight. It further observed that the airline had not furnished sufficient evidence to show that the family had received adequate meals.However, the commission took into account that the passengers had completed their journey and said a full ticket refund would be disproportionate.In an order dated October 7, it reduced the relief and directed Singapore Airlines to pay Rs 50,000 as consolidated compensation for mental agony and harassment, besides litigation expenses.The amount is to be paid to Singh within 45 days, Bar and Bench reported.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: A Virginia textile mill built in 1920 closed in 1996 and stood largely empty for decades; after a $110 million redevelopment, it now has residents and offices, with 190 apartments planned across the complex
articles.summary: The 1920-built White Mill in Danville, Virginia, operated for 75 years before closing in 1996.
articles.body: The 1920-built White Mill in Danville, Virginia, operated for 75 years before closing in 1996. Renamed Dan River Falls, the 650,000-square-foot historic complex is being transformed into apartments, offices, retail space and a riverfront community hub.A historic textile mill in Danville, Virginia, that once symbolised the city’s industrial prosperity has found a new purpose as a residential and commercial complex after decades of disuse. According to developer The Alexander Company, the former White Mill, built in 1920 and operated as Mill No. 8, is being redeveloped into Dan River Falls, a project valued at $110 million that combines 190 apartments with office space and retail facilities. The developer says the first residents moved in after the initial phase was completed in November 2024, while the redevelopment is scheduled for completion in 2026.The transformation reflects a broader effort to preserve Danville’s industrial heritage while bringing underused historic buildings back into economic and community life. The reinforced-concrete structure, which occupies more than 18 acres along the Dan River, is among the last surviving reminders of the city’s once-powerful textile manufacturing industry. Rather than demolishing the ageing mill, the redevelopment aims to retain its historic character while adapting its interiors for modern residential and commercial use.From textile production to a vacant industrial landmarkWhite Mill was built by Dan River Inc. in 1920 and began operating in 1921. Designed by Lockwood, Greene & Company, the five-storey building featured a simplified Gothic Revival architectural style and a distinctive reinforced-concrete structure. Its scale reflected the importance of textile manufacturing to Danville, where mills provided employment for generations of local families.The mill operated until 1996. As the textile industry declined, the building eventually stood largely idle, becoming a physical reminder of the economic changes that had reshaped the region. The decline of the wider textile industry cost Danville thousands of jobs, leaving former industrial properties struggling to find new uses.For decades, the White Mill remained a prominent feature along the riverfront, with the words “Home of Dan River Fabrics” once welcoming visitors arriving in the city. Its deteriorating condition presented a challenge: how could a vast industrial building be preserved without leaving it as an unused relic of the past? The answer came through a partnership between The Alexander Company, a Wisconsin-based historic redevelopment specialist, and the Danville Industrial Development Authority.A $110 million effort to preserve historyThe redevelopment effort began taking shape after years of discussions about how to reuse the property. In May 2021, Danville officials announced a partnership between the city’s Industrial Development Authority and The Alexander Company to convert White Mill into a mixed-use development. The original proposal called for 150 apartments and 110,000 square feet of commercial space in the first phase, with another 100 apartments planned for a later phase.Rehabilitation work began in December 2022. The project was subsequently named Dan River Falls, and the first phase was completed in November 2024. The developer's current plans list 190 apartments, 147,000 square feet of office space and a project completion date of 2026.The total investment is reported at approximately $110 million. According to Virginia Business, the redevelopment involved a public-private partnership in which The Alexander Company led the residential component, while the city and its partners oversaw commercial and public-facing elements. State and federal historic tax credits, alongside other financing arrangements, helped support the undertaking.Residents, offices and a new riverfront destinationThe apartments are not the only sign of the building's return to use. By October 2025, 150 apartments in the first phase had become home to more than 275 people, and another 40 units were being made available. The developer also says the housing includes options for workers earning less than 80% of the area's median income, linking the project to local workforce housing needs.The former mill is also accommodating public offices and private businesses. In early 2026, Danville's Office of Economic Development and Tourism moved into the complex, joining the city's Parks and Recreation department. Engineering and consulting firm Dewberry also relocated its Danville office to the property.The project extends beyond the mill's walls. Plans include a riverfront park, an extension of the city's Riverwalk Trail and space for retail and other commercial activities. The developer's website describes more than seven acres of riverfront parkland as part of the wider development vision.Preserving the original structure while adapting it for new uses has been central to the project. The work retains the building's reinforced-concrete framework and historic architectural character while creating interiors suited to modern living and working. The redevelopment was also recognised by Virginia Business as one of the state's notable projects in 2026, reflecting the scale of the conversion and the partnership behind it.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'You are disgusting, put yourself in shape': Trump mocks reporter's appearance after being questioned about his health
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump launched a personal attack on a journalist who questioned him about his health and the cancellation of planned campaign rallies
articles.body: US President Donald Trump launched a personal attack on a journalist who questioned him about his health and the cancellation of planned campaign rallies in Kansas and Iowa, telling the reporter to “put yourself in shape” and that he looked “like hell”.The exchange took place on Thursday when a reporter asked whether Trump’s decision not to travel to Kansas was linked to him feeling unwell after weeks of campaigning.Trump reacted angrily, telling the journalist, “Oh, you’re sick to ask that question. You are sick.”When the reporter clarified that he was asking about the President’s well-being, Trump turned to the journalist’s appearance. “Look at this guy. He’s way out of shape,” Trump said.Asked again about his health, Trump insisted he was fine. “I’ve been following me for two weeks. I feel perfect,” he said, before adding, “You are disgusting. Put yourself in shape. You look like hell.”The confrontation came as Trump cancelled planned weekend rallies in Kansas and Iowa, opting instead to address voters through phone rallies ahead of Tuesday’s midterm elections.Trump had been scheduled to campaign in Salina, Kansas, on Saturday and Dubuque, Iowa, on Sunday. Asked about skipping Kansas, he said he did not “feel like I have to go to Kansas” and expressed confidence in Republican Senator Roger Marshall’s prospects.The Republican National Committee (RNC) later confirmed the cancellation of the Iowa event as well. Trump’s campaign funding group, MAGA Inc., said it would organise phone rallies across nearly 20 states as part of a final push to support Republican candidates before Election Day.The cancellations come as Republicans face a difficult fight to retain their narrow control of both chambers of Congress, with several Senate races tightening in the final days of campaigning. Trump has held 25 rallies across 19 states in October, seeking to boost Republican candidates.Despite cancelling the two appearances, Trump is scheduled to travel to Daytona Beach, Florida, on Friday for another campaign event.Trump has previously acknowledged the physical demands of his campaign schedule. Speaking at a rally in Mississippi on Monday, he said, “God didn’t make your vocal cords to do a rally every day.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2026, a Massachusetts woman skied 700 miles to the South Pole alone, without support; she finished the frozen crossing in exactly 57 days
articles.summary: Monet Eliastam becomes the first American woman to complete a solo and unsupported ski journey to the South Pole, covering 700 miles in 57 days, facing extreme weather and challenging terrain.
articles.body: Monet Eliastam set off from Hercules Inlet on the edge of Antarctica on November 23, 2025, beginning her solo ski journey to the South Pole. She had to carry her food, shelter and equipment on sledges for 57 days on the Antarctic ice before reaching her destination on January 18, 2026. With this accomplishment, the Massachusetts native became the first American woman to ski solo and unsupported to the South Pole. According to the Boston Globe, Eliastam had spent nearly three years preparing for this expedition.A 700-mile journey across AntarcticaTravelling from the Ronne Ice Shelf across the Antarctic plateau towards the South Pole, Eliastam followed the Hercules Inlet route. The route is commonly described as around 700 miles, though Barnard College reported Eliastam’s completed distance as 702 miles. This difference only reflects the use of a rounded distance in coverage of the journey instead of a fundamentally different account of the expedition.Eliastam had to carry the provisions and equipment needed for survival on this quest. The combined weight of her pulk-sledge was around 250 pounds at the start of the journey, making each day’s progress physically demanding. Her every day routine included walking, eating, breaking camp, skiing for most of the day, and setting up shelter again when her day was done under the continuous polar sun. As per Barnard College, she usually skied for approximately 10 to 12 hours a day.In addition to the distance, the Antarctic environment posed further challenges. Eliastam encountered whiteouts, which made it hard to see sastrugi, ridges of wind-shaped snow, and powerful katabatic winds that sweep down from the continent’s high interior. On difficult days, uneven terrain and poor visibility prevented her from making further progress in her journey.Nearly three years of preparation were put into the expeditionAn alumna of Barnard College, Eliastam started preparing in earnest in 2023, mixing strength training with workouts that involved cardiovascular exercises designed to replicate the effort of hauling a heavy sledge. One interesting part of her training included dragging two large tyres across the beach and forest trails in North Shore, Massachusetts. The intention behind this particular exercise was to prepare her for dragging her supplies over Antarctic terrain.Her preparation also included a month-long expedition in Greenland with a group. She also had solo trips in Norway and Minnesota as part of her regimen. These experiences were instrumental in the development of skills for cold-weather travel, winter camping and managing equipment in remote conditions. The Boston Globe reported that the final stretch brought its own psychological strain during her South Pole expedition. On the 45th day, Eliastam navigated a landscape that was marked by prominent sastrugi and whiteout conditions. She had covered less ground than she had initially hoped. In her later accounts, she described feeling overwhelmed by the slow progress.What “solo” and “unsupported” mean in this expeditionThe terms “solo” and “unsupported” describe the conditions faced by the Massachusetts resident in her journey on the ice. She skied by herself and carried her own supplies without getting any resupply or physical assistance along the route. Though, this does not mean that the expedition had no logistical arrangements or emergency safeguards. Antarctic Logistics & Expeditions (ALE) organised the drop-off and operated within the wider expedition system. Eliastam maintained communications with them during the crossing. On January 18, 2026, Eliastam reached the South Pole after 57 days on ice. The Boston Globe reported that people came out of a tent and cheered as she arrived, before continuing to the ceremonial pole surrounded by flags.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: First Mahatma Gandhi statue in North Dakota unveiled at Bismarck's Peace Park
articles.summary: The first life-size statue of Mahatma Gandhi in North Dakota was unveiled at Peace Park in downtown Bismarck, the state's capital, in a ceremony attended
articles.body: The first life-size statue of Mahatma Gandhi in North Dakota was unveiled at Peace Park in downtown Bismarck, the state's capital, in a ceremony attended by the state's first lady Kjersti Armstrong and agriculture commissioner Doug Goehring.The statue was installed with the assistance of the Consulate General of India in Seattle, with technical support from the Indian American community in North Dakota and the North Dakota Trade Office, the consulate said in a press release.The unveiling ceremony began with the national anthems of India and the United States, followed by musical renditions of Gandhi's favourite hymns by school students from North Dakota. Officials from the Bismarck Parks and Recreation District and members of the Indian American community also attended the event.The unveiling took place during the month of Gandhi Jayanti, observed worldwide on October 2 as the International Day of Non-Violence. It also marked the year of Gandhi's 157th birth anniversary.Addressing the gathering, North Dakota agriculture commissioner Doug Goehring highlighted the growing friendship between India and North Dakota. He said Gandhi's message resonated not only with India and the rest of the world but also with people in North Dakota.Goehring described the statue as a symbol of peace and non-violence and recalled Gandhi's timeless message.North Dakota first lady Kjersti Armstrong expressed her admiration for Gandhi, saying it was an honour to celebrate his legacy, which she described as being more important today than it had been in a very long time.Peace Park adds Gandhi statue to public art installationsLocated at 400 East Front Avenue in downtown Bismarck, Peace Park was developed shortly after the September 11, 2001, attacks. It is also home to a Peace Pole installed by the Gandhi Peace Network of North Dakota, along with other bronze sculptural artefacts.The Gandhi statue joins these installations, adding to the public art heritage of North Dakota's capital city. The consulate described Gandhi's life and message as universal symbols of peace and non-violence.The installation also comes amid growing engagement between India and North Dakota since the establishment of the Consulate General of India in Seattle.According to the consulate, visits by the Consul General to North Dakota in 2024 and 2026 included meetings with the governor, the mayor of Bismarck and leaders from the agriculture, business and education sectors.The consulate has also organised cultural and consular outreach programmes in Fargo, including the International Day of Yoga 2026 and a consular camp in February 2026. Senior delegates from the North Dakota Trade Office also visited India earlier this year as part of ongoing exchanges between the two sides.Fifth Gandhi monument under Seattle consulate's jurisdictionThe Bismarck installation is the latest addition to the Consulate General of India's initiative to establish Gandhi monuments across the US Pacific North and Midwest.Earlier statues were installed at the base of the Space Needle in Seattle in October 2024, at the State Capitol in Lincoln, Nebraska, in December 2024, and at the Mansfield Center at the University of Montana in Missoula in March 2026.Along with the statue installed at Bellevue Public Library in October 2009, the Bismarck monument is the fifth Mahatma Gandhi statue within the jurisdiction of the Consulate General of India in Seattle, the press release said.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Austrian electrical engineer left IT after visiting US national parks, became a ranger, and now oversees trails and infrastructure at Gesäuse National Park
articles.summary: Markus Blank transitions from a 13-year IT career to park ranger, overseeing maintenance and trails at Gesäuse National Park in Austria after inspiration from US national parks.
articles.body: After working 13 years in the information technology sector, Austrian electrical engineering graduate Markus Blank opted to pursue a different career path. A visit to national parks in the United States helped him realise that he wanted to become a park ranger. He later volunteered at the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area in California before returning to Austria. After returning, he joined Gesäuse National Park. According to a profile published by the US National Park Service (NPS) in July 2022, Blank later became the park’s chief of maintenance, overseeing its infrastructure and maintenance staff.Transition from information technology to park rangerMarkus Blank studied electrical engineering and went on to manage information technology departments at several medium-sized companies. Though he had built a career in this industry, he eventually concluded that it was not something he wanted to do for the rest of his life. After working for 13 years, he left his previous professional path and began considering his next venture. A subsequent trip to US national parks helped him identify his next ambition, that is, working as a park ranger.To gather practical knowledge and experience, Blank contacted the international volunteer coordinator at the NPS Office of International Affairs. He secured a volunteer position at Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area in California. There, he was presented with the opportunity to learn about the different aspects of national park operations. In an earlier interview published by National Parks Austria, Blank mentioned that his year there exposed him to areas including environmental education, visitor services, park law enforcement, maintenance and conservation. He shared that interpreting nature and communicating environmental information to visitors in particular interested him.After returning to Austria, Blank applied for a ranger position at Gesäuse National Park, located in the country’s Styria region. The NPS profile mentions that he spent several years interpreting the park’s natural and cultural resources for the public before moving into the chief of maintenance role. His progression thus illustrates how his initial interest in ranger work evolved into experience in both visitor education and the operational side of managing a protected area.Overseeing trails and park infrastructure In its 2022 profile, the US agency described Blank as responsible for the park’s man-made structures and infrastructure alongside its maintenance staff. Buildings, trails, information boards, signs, visitor way-sides, parking areas and climate stations are all listed facilities that fall under his role.Gesäuse National Park protects a mountainous landscape shaped by the Enns River and the limestone peaks of the Austrian Alps. According to National Parks Austria, it is the only national park in Styria, with habitats including forests, rocky slopes, alpine grasslands and waterways. The general profile of the park rounds its size to approximately 12,000 hectares.Notably, maintaining trails, signs and visitor facilities is one part of the broader work involved in managing such a landscape. In addition to this, the park has ranger activities connected with visitor information, environmental education and conservation. Rangers have been described as people who communicate information about the protected area and serve as contacts for visitors on the park’s official website.An international perspective on conservation workThe NPS featured Blank in its article Celebrating Park Rangers Around the Globe on World Ranger Day, published in July 2022. Annually observed on July 31, World Ranger Day recognises the work put in by rangers in protecting natural and cultural heritage. The day also commemorates those killed or injured in the line of duty. The July 2022 article presented professionals from several countries to showcase the range of work involved in managing protected areas around the world.Blank’s career move from IT to national park work eventually led him into a position overseeing the facilities and staff responsible for maintaining park infrastructure. The 2022 profile documents the transition from the technical private sector to a leadership role within a protected landscape. Additionally, it highlights that a ranger's career can involve different responsibilities.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Jupiter Transit in Leo 2026 for Aries/Mesha Ascendant: Children, higher studies, father, foreign travel and income come into focus
articles.summary: A parent stands at a college admission counter with a file of mark sheets, photocopies of every certificate and a slightly damp handkerchief.
articles.body: A parent stands at a college admission counter with a file of mark sheets, photocopies of every certificate and a slightly damp handkerchief. The clerk says the list goes up on Monday. Anyone who has stood in that queue knows the feeling, and it is the feeling this transit brings to the forefront of your chart.When Jupiter moves into Leo, it lands in your 5th house, the house of children, college education, intelligence and planning.Jupiter enters Leo on 31 October 2026 (one panchang, the Hindu almanac, gives 1 November) and stays until 25 January 2027, turning retrograde on 13 December. All dates here follow the sidereal, or Lahiri, panchang, so check your local panchang for the exact hour.For Aries ascendant, Jupiter rules your 9th house, Sagittarius, and your 12th house, Pisces. The headline is the 9th house. From Leo, Jupiter aspects Sagittarius with its 5th aspect, while Saturn, sitting in Pisces, aspects the same sign with its 10th aspect. Two heavy planets, one house.Why the 5th house is suddenly crowdedJupiter is not exalted in Leo. That was Cancer, your 4th house, where matters relating to home and family fell into place almost on their own. Leo belongs to the Sun, a friend of Jupiter, so Jupiter is comfortable and respected here. But it asks for visibility, effort and a little authority from you.The 5th house covers children, their education, intelligence, foresight, love affairs, pregnancy, literature and speculation. Expect decisions about a child's course, college admission, marriage prospects or future to come up at your dining table. If you are the one applying for a seat or a programme, doors can open. Some of you will see a romance move towards a real commitment, while couples hoping for pregnancy or undergoing fertility treatment may find the subject becoming more urgent.Teachers, writers, planners and anyone who works with ideas tend to get a good run. Start the manuscript, draft the syllabus or outline the business plan. Speculation is a different matter. A lit-up house does not guarantee a profit, so keep share-market tips and lottery-style schemes at arm's length.Where the Jupiter-Saturn pressure builds: the 9th houseThis is the longest part of the story, so settle in. The 9th house represents your father, guru, spiritual guide and teachers, as well as fortune, religion, charity, virtuous deeds, pilgrimage, long journeys, courts, postgraduate study, emigration and immigration. Jupiter makes whatever it touches bigger, which is good news until the paperwork starts piling up.Saturn tightens and delays. Put them together in one house and you get growth that comes with a queue.So, a master's admission, an advanced professional qualification or a mentor who finally takes you seriously could be on the cards, but the form may need a second signature. A pilgrimage may be planned for months before the tickets are booked. A visa or immigration application could reach an important stage, and a court case or a legal question concerning an inheritance may come up for a hearing, though not necessarily a verdict.Saturn is retrograde until around 11 December (some panchangs say 14 December), so expect the first six weeks to feel slower than the weeks that follow, with more movement once Saturn turns direct.Your father's health, work or responsibilities may need your attention, too. That is a theme of the house, not a medical diagnosis, and no transit can tell you what is wrong with anyone. Spend an evening with him, ask about his files and go through his papers. Saturn rewards the child who takes care of the dull administrative work early.Since Jupiter also rules your 12th house, some of the foreign or long-distance movement may involve additional spending. Budget for it.Money and friends from the Aquarius cornerJupiter's 7th aspect falls on Aquarius, your 11th house. This is the house of income, gains, fulfilment of ambitions, elder siblings, friends, family business and important documents. It is also associated with recovery from illness.Watch for a payment that has been stuck for a year finally clearing, an old dues settlement being closed or a contact bringing you a new client. Your network can widen, and an elder brother or sister may need your support or offer you theirs.Family reputation matters here, so be careful about what you sign and what you say at weddings. Keep photocopies of every property or business document, because this house likes paperwork.Your own face in the mirrorJupiter's 9th aspect falls on Aries itself, your 1st house. It supports vitality, self-respect and confidence, and encourages you to improve your circumstances. It also nudges you to reconsider your overall direction in life.Some of you will join a gym or finally settle into a routine. Others will think about how the world sees them, from their LinkedIn profile to their haircut. If a job offer or a move to another city is on the table, make your decision on paper rather than in a rush.What happens when Jupiter turns around on 13 December?Because the first Leo phase lasts less than three months and Jupiter turns retrograde midway through it, anything you begin in November may need a review, a follow-up or a second attempt in December and January. That is normal.Apply early, submit your documents twice and keep the receipt.Jupiter moves back into Cancer, still retrograde, on 25 January 2027 and returns to Leo on 26 June 2027. The themes above will come back then with greater weight.Your birth chart and the dasha you are going through, the planetary period currently running in your life, will determine how strongly this transit affects you. The transit alone does not tell the whole story.Remedies for a crowded 9th houseTradition says that when the 9th house is in focus, you should honour the people it represents. Serve your father, touch the feet of your teachers and, if a guru or elder has guided you, give them a call.Many families read or listen to the Vishnu Sahasranama, a thousand names of Vishnu, on Thursdays. These are customs, not guarantees.For Jupiter itself, the following mantras are traditionally chanted 108 times on Thursday mornings:ॐ ग्रां ग्रीं ग्रौं सः गुरवे नमः (Om Graam Greem Graum Sah Gurave Namah)ॐ बृं बृहस्पतये नमः (Om Brim Brihaspataye Namah)Daan, the traditional act of giving, includes chana dal (split chickpeas), turmeric, jaggery (unrefined cane sugar), bananas, ghee (clarified butter), yellow cloth, and books or stationery for students.Given the 5th-house connection, donating a pile of notebooks to a needy child for the new academic term is a sensible choice. Many people also wear yellow, eat a light sattvic (simple, pure) meal and offer water to a banana tree on Thursdays.This coming Thursday, pull out the admission, visa or property file you have been avoiding. Sort it, make two photocopies, write down the missing document on a sticky note and light a ghee lamp before you begin.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: In 2011, Oregon biology professor Helen Stafford left Reed College $8 million; most went to student aid, while $1 million supported the department
articles.summary: Explore the legacy of Helen Stafford, the influential Reed College biology professor whose $8 million bequest significantly supports student aid and the biology department, ensuring a lasting impact on future generations of students.
articles.body: Reed College is a small liberal arts college in Portland, Oregon, and its biology department has had a reputation for combining lab research with teaching for decades. Among those who helped establish this reputation is Helen Stafford, a plant physiologist who spent most of her professional career at Reed.Stafford lived modestly and remained connected with the college even after retirement. Upon the settling of her estate, it became obvious that Stafford’s connection with Reed College was not limited to the classroom. Her bequest has had a significant impact on the college’s ability to support students who cannot afford to attend Reed.Helen Stafford’s route from Wellesley to Reed faculty Reed Magazine’s December 2011 feature “Bio Prof Bequeaths Fortune to Reed,” by Randall S. Barton, reports that Stafford was born in Philadelphia in 1922 and attended Wellesley College on a scholarship, studying botany. Reed’s archives add that she received her bachelor’s degree from Wellesley in 1944, her master’s from Connecticut College in 1948 and her doctorate from the University of Pennsylvania in 1951. She started working at Reed in 1954 and, as the same feature describes it, became the college’s first female professor in the sciences. Pamela Ronald, who was once a student and is now a professor of plant pathology at UC Davis, wrote on the science blog Biofortified that Stafford faced limited opportunities as a female scientist in the 1950s and that Reed hired her.Two Plant Physiology papers that show the range of her researchStafford also published extensively in the journal Plant Physiology, and the college archives mention her membership on the journal’s editorial board. She published Factors controlling the synthesis of natural and induced lignins in Phleum and Elodea in 1965; the article is in volume 40, number 5, pp. 844 to 851 of the journal. It discussed the process by which plants synthesize lignin, which is a complex molecule that makes the cell wall rigid. In 1958, Stafford co-authored The fixation of CO₂ into tartaric and malic acids of excised grape leaves with Frank Loewus; it appeared in volume 33, number 3, pp. 194 to 199 of the journal and was about carbon dioxide fixation into two organic acids in excised grape leaves.Reed’s finding aid for the Helen A. Stafford papers records that she served as president of the Phytochemical Society of North America from 1977 to 1978, published the book Flavonoid Metabolism in 1990, and received the Phytochemistry Pioneer Award in 2008. Reed’s 2021 story on the biology mural adds that she was the first Reed professor to win a Guggenheim Fellowship and received continuous NSF funding for over 30 years.The $8 million gift with $1 million set aside for biologyThe December 2011 feature also reports that Stafford left $8 million to the college through her will. The bulk of the gift provides financial aid for students who would otherwise be unable to attend, and $1 million supports the biology department. President Colin Diver announced the bequest as the Centennial Campaign passed $185 million toward its $200 million goal. The campaign, launched in 2005 and scheduled to conclude in December 2012, finished with gifts totalling more than $200 million, as Reed Magazine’s March 2011 and March 2013 issues show. The gift also supports summer fellowships for biology students, a point the 2021 mural story makes. The same feature separately says she endowed the $1 million Morton O. Stafford Jr. scholarship in memory of her brother, who was killed in World War II, though it does not say whether that scholarship came out of the financial aid share of the bequest or was a separate allocation.Her ties to campus after retiringReed Magazine’s June 2012 issue adds that Stafford continued advising her thesis students for years after she retired. Her caretaker, Mary Potts, said Stafford used to visit campus five days a week, and that her ashes were scattered at the lakeshore near the bridge she loved. In 2021, students and professors in the biology department, working with a visiting artist, painted a mural honoring her in the north stairwell of the biology building, as Reed’s story on the project reports.You use AI every day. articles.title: Google sees its worst day in 20 years, but why it may not be alone
articles.summary: Google-parent Alphabet witnessed its worst stock market performance in more than 20 years on Thursday, October 29.
articles.body: Google-parent Alphabet witnessed its worst stock market performance in more than 20 years on Thursday, October 29. The company’s shares plunged 12.6% following its latest earnings report. The decline wiped out around $500 billion in Alphabet's market value. Announcing the Q3 results, Alphabet said that it burned through more cash during the quarter, according to a measure called free cash flow, after its purchases of property and equipment topped $51 billion. However, the company may not be alone in facing investor concerns, as the massive cost of building AI infrastructure is putting pressure on the cash flow of major technology companies. Other tech giants, including Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Oracle, are also committing billions of dollars to AI development, data centres and computing infrastructure.Why did Google's stock suffer its worst fall in 20 yearsAlphabet's Class A shares fell 12.6% on October 29, marking their worst single-day decline since they began trading more than two decades ago. The fall came after the company reported weaker-than-expected growth for the summer quarter, adding to concerns over its rising AI expenditure.According to the Associated Press, Alphabet's purchases of property and equipment crossed $51 billion during the latest quarter, while its free cash flow turned negative. Free cash flow refers to the money a company has left after paying for its operating expenses and capital investments. It is an important measure of how much cash a business can generate after funding its expansion.The concern is not limited to how much Google is spending, but also how quickly it can recover that money through its AI and cloud businesses. With major technology companies racing to build data centres and secure AI computing capacity, investors are increasingly looking at whether the returns from these investments can keep pace with the rising costs.Why Google's AI spending concerns may not be limited to AlphabetAs mentioned above, Alphabet is not the only technology company spending heavily to build AI infrastructure. Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Oracle are also investing billions of dollars in data centres, servers, chips and cloud computing capacity to support their AI ambitions.A Reuters analysis published in July found that five major cloud infrastructure companies, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle, could collectively spend more on capital expenditure than they generate in free cash flow by 2027, based on LSEG consensus estimates. The analysis estimated that their combined capital expenditure could increase by around $534 billion between 2025 and 2027, while their annual operating cash flow could rise by approximately $340 billion over the same period.This highlights the financial pressure that could emerge as companies continue expanding their AI infrastructure. Even when AI-related revenue grows, the cost of building and maintaining the infrastructure needed to support these services could consume a significant portion of the cash generated by their businesses.Amazon, Meta are also facing AI spending scrutinyAmazon is among the biggest spenders in the AI infrastructure race. The company said it remains on track to spend around $220 billion on capital expenditure in 2026, with a significant portion directed towards AI infrastructure. CEO Andy Jassy has defended the investment, saying spending on Amazon Web Services is delivering growth.Meta has also faced investor concerns over its AI expenditure. The company recently raised its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to between $135 billion and $145 billion. Its increased spending outlook overshadowed stronger-than-expected revenue growth, highlighting investor concerns about how quickly its AI investments will translate into financial returns.You use AI every day. articles.title: Community Connect: Chennai gets into the halloween spirit
articles.summary: Forget vampires, witches and the usual Halloween suspects.
articles.body: Forget vampires, witches and the usual Halloween suspects. As October draws to a close, the city’s house parties are getting a distinctly Kollywood makeover (why be Miranda Priestly when you can be Neelambari?). Meanwhile, others are gearing up for horror movie marathons, VR horror rides, themed dining experiences and even a storytelling session.Kollywood characters & spooky living roomsFor this group of Chennai friends, Halloween is getting a Kollywood twist. Organiser Arjun says guests will dress as Tamil cinema characters, from a Jailer 2's MVP to Karuppu, while one couple plans to recreate Rishikanth and Anishma’s looks from Modha Rathiri. “We wanted to make Halloween a little more fun this year, so we’re bringing Tamil cinema into the mix. There are prizes for the top three costumes, with vouchers and a special hamper up for grabs,” he says.Meanwhile, research analyst Sashka and her friends are continuing their annual horror movie night, screening Insidious alongside a creepy-themed potluck. The menu? Finger-shaped sausages, eyeball devilled eggs, ‘witches’ blood’ mocktails and gummy-worm brownies. “The movie is only half the fun; the other half is seeing what everyone brings. The more disgusting it looks, the better!” she laughs.City’s Halloween scene goes beyond themed partiesFrom Halloween-themed buffets and DJ nights to virtual reality horror rides and ghost stories, the city has a spooky line-up this week. Ministry of Chutneys at Radisson Blu Hotel & Suites GRT Chennai has been celebrating the event from October 25 onwards. “Halloween offers a playful way to bring families and friends together,” says Vikram Cotah, its CEO, adding that younger audiences are increasingly open to themed dining and entertainment. At The Park, Nungambakkam, Six ’O’ One (601) is hosting a Halloween-themed dinner buffet, while Pasha will feature special cocktails, themed décor and a DJ party. “The celebrations offer guests an opportunity to enjoy different Halloween experiences, from a themed dining experience to an evening of music and entertainment, all at one destination,” says a hotel representative.At Alliance Française of Madras, October 30 and 31 will feature virtual reality horror rides at La Maison Café Library and Tell Me a Scary Story, a storytelling session at Espace 24. An interactive discussion comparing French and Indian myths and superstitions is also scheduled for October 31.Paws, paint and pumpkinsHalloween got a particularly adorable twist at a recent pumpkin-painting session, where participants painted pumpkin cut-outs in the company of playful puppies. “It was such a fun way to spend an evening. We came expecting to paint pumpkins, but the puppies completely stole the show. Everyone was taking pictures, exchanging colours and trying to get the little ones to sit still. It felt less like an event and more like hanging out with friends,” says Dev Thakkar, a research analyst.Financial advisor Ojaswita Saha adds, “The best part was how relaxed everything felt. You could be terrible at painting and still have the best time. The puppies made the whole experience so much sweeter, and honestly, it was the kind of Halloween plan I would happily sign up for again.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: An Ohio man bought a house in a neighbourhood of about 140 homes and advertised it on Airbnb, arguing it was also his residence; on October 26, an appeals court upheld a zoning ban after neighbours objected
articles.summary: An Ohio appeals court has upheld a local zoning ban on short-term home rentals.
articles.body: An Ohio appeals court has upheld a local zoning ban on short-term home rentals. The ruling shuts down a property owner’s attempt to run an Airbnb business in a quiet suburban neighborhood of about 140 homes. In a decision issued on 26 October 2026, the Fifth District Court of Appeals of Ohio backed a lower court ruling against home buyer Michael A. Clevenger. The court found that local residential zoning rules legally bar short-term tourist rentals run as a business in single-family zones. The dispute began after Clevenger bought a single-family house in a housing development of about 140 properties in Stark County, Ohio. Soon after he took ownership, he listed the house on online booking sites. He advertised it for short stays to passing guests and vacationers. Nearby residents quickly raised concerns about crowded parking, noise, and safety risks. Local zoning inspectors then issued a formal notice of violation. They said he was running an unapproved business in an area zoned only for single-family homes. Clevenger appealed the enforcement action to the local township zoning board. He then appealed to the Stark County Court of Common Pleas. He argued that renting out the house did not break the zoning code. He said the house was his main home and that he only sometimes hosted guests.Rejection of primary residence argumentThe Fifth District Court of Appeals rejected Clevenger’s arguments one by one. It held that short-term commercial rentals change the basic residential character of a neighborhood. This is true even if the owner sometimes sleeps at the property. The court wrote for its three-judge panel that local township zoning codes exist to protect stable, quiet, low-density living for long-term residents. Court records show that neighbors gave local authorities logs, photographs, and testimony. These described frequent guest turnover, parties, and unfamiliar cars parked along narrow residential streets. The appeals judges decided that advertising a house for paid short stays turns a single-family home into a hotel-style business. That kind of business needs specific commercial zoning approval or a conditional use permit. The property had neither. The court also ruled that the local zoning board acted within its legal powers when it read the township land-use codes. It confirmed that local governments in Ohio have clear police powers to limit short-term rentals. These powers protect neighborhood safety and property values.Growing legal precedent on short-term rentalsThe 26 October ruling adds to a series of similar decisions in Ohio state courts. Those decisions back the right of local towns and township trustees to limit or ban platforms like Airbnb and VRBO in established residential areas. Lawyers for local homeowners argued during court hearings that unmonitored commercial rentals in a subdivision of 140 homes would badly weaken deed restrictions and local land planning rules. Those rules are meant to build long-term community ties. Under Ohio law, township trustees have broad power to define land uses within set zones. Courts have repeatedly held that short-term rentals do not count as normal single-family residential use. This is because guests do not live there permanently or sign long-term leases. The decision makes clear that property owners cannot avoid local short-term rental bans by simply calling a property their personal residence while actively offering rooms to paying travelers. Clevenger can still ask the Supreme Court of Ohio for a discretionary review. However, state legal experts consider it unlikely that further appeals would overturn the settled precedent on local township land-use powers.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A $295 million Malibu mansion by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Tadao Ando was quietly on the market when Kanye West came unannounced and stayed for four days, a new book claims; his own Ando-designed Malibu home now faces an uncertain future
articles.summary: A $295 million Malibu mansion designed by Pritzker Prize-winning Japanese architect Tadao Ando was quietly on the market when rapper Kanye West arrived
articles.body: A $295 million Malibu mansion designed by Pritzker Prize-winning Japanese architect Tadao Ando was quietly on the market when rapper Kanye West arrived unannounced and stayed for four days, according to a new biography of his former wife, Kim Kardashian. An October 2026 report by the New York Post drew on journalist Jonathan Van Meter’s book 'Citizen Kim' to recount how West persuaded the estate’s owners to let him inside, set up an office beside the pool and hold meetings there. The episode offers a glimpse into the rapper’s fascination with Ando’s architecture, even as West’s own Ando-designed Malibu property remains mired in restoration and foreclosure complications.Kanye West’s unexpected visit to the $295 million estateArt collectors Maria and Bill Bell commissioned the mansion in Malibu’s exclusive Paradise Cove area. Known as the “Big Ando”, the approximately 42,000-square-foot property took 15 years to build and features the Japanese architect’s signature use of concrete, geometric forms and carefully framed ocean views. According to 'Citizen Kim', West drove to the estate without scheduling an appointment through celebrity real estate agent Kurt Rappaport, who represented the owners. Instead, he reportedly arrived at the gate and introduced himself.When the owner hesitated to let him in, West allegedly invoked Elvis Presley to make his case. “If Elvis Presley came to your door and rang your buzzer, would you let him in? This is that,” he reportedly said. The visit went far beyond a conventional property viewing. Van Meter writes that West remained at the estate for four days, setting up an office by the pool and holding meetings because he wanted to experience what it felt like to work inside an Ando-designed home.The mansion had reportedly been marketed privately for $295 million. It was eventually purchased by Jay-Z and Beyoncé in 2023 for $200 million, setting a California residential real estate sales record at the time. The sale price was substantially below the reported asking price.The smaller Ando house West bought for $57.25 millionThe larger estate was not West’s first encounter with the architect’s work. In September 2021, he purchased a separate oceanfront house on Malibu Road for $57.25 million. The roughly 4,000-square-foot residence had originally been commissioned by financier and art collector Richard Sachs and was completed in 2013 after a seven-year design and construction process. It was also designed by Ando, whose limited portfolio of standalone residential buildings in the United States makes the properties particularly notable among architecture enthusiasts.According to the New York Post, Ando’s executive architect for the Malibu Road project, Ron Radziner, used the informal name “Little Ando” for West’s house, distinguishing it from the much larger Paradise Cove estate. West reportedly wanted to turn his own property into an intensely minimalist retreat, described in media reports as a bunker, bomb shelter or “bat cave”. But the renovation took a destructive turn, leaving the home without many of the features required for ordinary habitation.From architectural landmark to an unfinished concrete shellAfter purchasing the Malibu Road house, West hired contractor Tony Saxon to carry out the renovation. The work involved removing windows, plumbing, electrical systems, marble bathrooms and other interior features. The changes stripped the residence of much of its original design and left an unfinished concrete structure exposed to the coastal environment. The alterations also triggered a legal dispute. Saxon sued West for $1.7 million over the renovation project. According to the New York Post, a Los Angeles jury awarded Saxon $140,000 in March 2026 for lost wages and medical expenses. West eventually abandoned the project and listed the property in December 2023 for $53 million. The house sold in September 2024 for $21 million to developer Steven “Bo” Belmont’s real estate firm, Belwood Investments.The new owner initially pledged to restore the residence to its original design. In March 2025, however, the partly renovated house returned to the market with an asking price of $39 million. Belmont said at the time that approximately $2 million in restoration work had been completed and estimated that another $6.5 million would be needed.Foreclosure delays leave the property's future uncertainThe restoration plans encountered further difficulties after the property’s ownership company faced foreclosure proceedings. A December 2025 report by Realtor.com said the lender had accused Belwood Investments of defaulting on an $18.5 million mortgage and sought to recover overdue payments. The foreclosure auction was subsequently postponed. According to Realtor.com’s April 7, 2026, report, an auction scheduled for March 19 was halted after a last-minute bankruptcy filing. A second scheduled sale on April 7 was also postponed, with no new date immediately announced.Belmont maintained that he was working towards completing the restoration and protecting investors’ interests. The delays left the property’s ultimate fate unresolved in the latest reports available for this account.The two Malibu houses illustrate sharply different outcomes for Ando’s work. The larger Paradise Cove estate became a record-breaking purchase for Beyoncé and Jay-Z, while West’s smaller property remains caught between architectural restoration and financial uncertainty.Ando, who received the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 1995, is known for using exposed concrete, natural light and restrained forms to create spaces that interact closely with their surroundings. His Malibu residences were designed around those principles. Whether the smaller house can be restored to its original vision remains an open question.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision?
